title: Swapping Nodes in a Linked List Problem

content.problemStatement:
A singly linked list is given to you as an array `nums`, where `nums[i]` is the value of the i-th node in order.

**Swap the value of the `k`th node from the beginning with the value of the `k`th node from the end (both 1-indexed), then return the resulting list's values in order.**

The two nodes may be the same node, in which case the swap is a no-op. Either way, only values are swapped, the list's structure and length stay the same.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: the 2nd node from the start (value 2) and the 2nd node from the end (value 4) swap values
the 1st node from the start and the 1st from the end are the same single node

code.Python3:
# Time:  O(n)
# Space: O(1)

# Definition for singly-linked list.
class ListNode(object):
    def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
        pass


class Solution(object):
    def swapNodes(self, head, k):
        """
        :type head: ListNode
        :type k: int
        :rtype: ListNode
        """
        left, right, curr = None, None, head
        while curr:
            k -= 1
            if right:
                right = right.next
            if k == 0:
                left = curr
                right = head
            curr = curr.next
        left.val, right.val = right.val, left.val
        return head
